context_summary: F05 Technical Debt Cleanup — plan-feature (Architect only, PLAN_ONLY). Feature resolves accumulated tech debt: test coverage gaps (provider.py 63%, parsers 82%, CLI 77%), missing PRDs (F02/F03/F04), missing F04 diagrams, .coverage in .gitignore, stale F03 status. No new modules or architectural changes. Purely additive (tests, docs, config). Overall coverage target: 90%. Architect already produced 6 tasks in 3 waves.

options_considered.description: Accept the existing Architect plan as-is: 6 tasks, 3 waves (W0: housekeeping, W1: test coverage x3 parallel, W2: docs x2 parallel). PLAN_ONLY — no execution.
pros: Tasks are well-scoped with clear ACs and measurable targets
Wave ordering is correct: housekeeping first, then independent test tasks in parallel, then independent doc tasks in parallel
No architectural risk — only adding tests, docs, and config
Coverage targets are reasonable (85-90%) and achievable
cons: 6 tasks for housekeeping/debt may be over-decomposed — could merge T05+T06 into one docs task
Minor: line numbers in task descriptions may drift if code changes before execution

options_considered.description: Re-plan with fewer tasks: merge docs tasks (T05+T06), merge parser+CLI tests (T03+T04).
pros: Docs are all documentation artifacts, could be one task
cons: T03 and T04 test different modules with different complexity — keeping separate is cleaner
T05 (PRDs) and T06 (diagrams) are different artifact types
Existing plan is already well-specified — re-planning wastes effort
Wave 1 and Wave 2 already run tasks in parallel, so task count doesn't affect execution time

rationale: The existing Architect plan is well-structured. 6 tasks with clear scope, measurable coverage targets, and correct wave dependencies. No architectural risk since this is purely additive (tests, docs, config). The decomposition allows parallel execution in Waves 1 and 2. Re-planning would waste effort with no material improvement.
